title: Post-Incorporation Compliances & Bank Account Setup
question_text: Within how many days from the date of incorporation must a company with share capital file Form INC-20A (Declaration of Commencement of Business)?
explanation: Section 10A(1)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013 stipulates that Form INC-20A must be filed with the ROC within 180 days from the date of incorporation.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 10A, Companies Act, 2013 & Rule 23A of Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014

title: First Board Meeting & Secretarial Standard-1 (SS-1)
question_text: Under Section 173(1), within what timeframe must every newly incorporated company hold its first Board of Directors meeting?
explanation: Section 173(1) mandates that every company shall hold the first meeting of the Board of Directors within thirty days of the date of its incorporation.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 173(1), Companies Act, 2013 & ICSI Secretarial Standard-1 (SS-1)

title: Appointment of First Statutory Auditor (Form ADT-1)
question_text: If the Board of Directors fails to appoint the first statutory auditor within 30 days of incorporation, within how many days must members appoint the auditor at an EGM?
topic_name: Appointment of First Statutory Auditor (Form ADT-1)
explanation: Section 139(6) provides that if the Board fails to appoint the first auditor within 30 days, members of the company shall appoint within 90 days at an EGM.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 139(6), Companies Act, 2013 & Rule 4(2) of Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014

title: Share Certificate Issuance & State Stamp Duty
question_text: Under Section 56(4)(a), within what maximum timeframe must share certificates be delivered to subscribers from the date of incorporation?
topic_name: Share Certificate Issuance & State Stamp Duty
explanation: Section 56(4)(a) mandates delivery of share certificates to subscribers within 2 months (60 days) from the date of incorporation.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 56(4), Companies Act, 2013 & Indian Stamp Act, 1899

title: Director Disqualifications, DIN & Annual DIR-3 KYC
question_text: Under Section 164(2)(a), what continuous period of default in filing financial statements or annual returns triggers a 5-year director disqualification?
topic_name: Director Disqualifications, DIN & Annual DIR-3 KYC
explanation: Section 164(2)(a) provides that failure to file financial statements or annual returns for any continuous period of 3 financial years results in disqualification for 5 years.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 164(2), Section 167 & Rule 12A of Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014

title: Related Party Transactions & Approvals (Section 188)
question_text: Which of the following related party contracts is EXEMPT from Board and General Meeting approval under Section 188(1)?

options.text: Transactions entered in ordinary course of business on an arm's length basis
Contracts approved verbally by the Managing Director

explanation: Section 188(1) fourth proviso explicitly states that nothing in this sub-section shall apply to any transactions entered into by the company in its ordinary course of business other than transactions which are not on an arm’s length basis.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 188 & Section 177, Companies Act, 2013 & Rule 15 of Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014

option_b: Transactions entered in ordinary course of business on an arm's length basis
option_d: Contracts approved verbally by the Managing Director

title: Board Meetings, Quorum & Video Conferencing
question_text: What is the maximum permissible time gap between two consecutive Board Meetings under Section 173(1)?
explanation: Section 173(1) mandates that not more than one hundred and twenty (120) days shall intervene between two consecutive meetings of the Board.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 173, Section 174 & Rule 3 of Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014

title: General Meetings & Secretarial Standard-2 (SS-2)
question_text: What is the statutory notice period required for calling an Annual General Meeting under Section 101(1)?
explanation: Section 101(1) requires that a general meeting of a company may be called by giving not less than clear twenty-one days’ notice either in writing or through electronic mode.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 96, Section 100, Section 101, Companies Act, 2013 & ICSI Secretarial Standard-2 (SS-2)

title: Loans to Directors & Inter-Corporate Investments (Sec 185/186)
question_text: What is the ceiling threshold under Section 186(2) beyond which inter-corporate loans and investments require prior approval by Special Resolution?

options.text: 60% of paid-up capital + free reserves + securities premium (or 100% of free reserves + securities premium)

explanation: Section 186(2) provides that no company shall directly or indirectly give loan/investment exceeding 60% of paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium, or 100% of free reserves and securities premium, whichever is higher, without Special Resolution.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 185 & Section 186, Companies Act, 2013 & Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014

option_b: 60% of paid-up capital + free reserves + securities premium (or 100% of free reserves + securities premium)

title: Acceptance of Deposits & Annual Form DPT-3
question_text: What is the mandatory annual deadline for filing Form DPT-3 (Return of Deposits / Particulars of Transactions not considered as Deposit) with the ROC?
topic_name: Acceptance of Deposits & Annual Form DPT-3
explanation: Rule 16 of Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules mandates that Form DPT-3 must be filed on or before the 30th day of June every year with information as on 31st March.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 73 to 76, Companies Act, 2013 & Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014

title: Annual Filings: Form AOC-4 & Financial Statements
question_text: Within how many days from the date of the AGM must Form AOC-4 (Financial Statements) be filed with the ROC?
topic_name: Annual Filings: Form AOC-4 & Financial Statements
explanation: Section 137(1) requires that financial statements adopted at the AGM shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the date of the annual general meeting.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 137, Companies Act, 2013 & Rule 12 of Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014

title: Annual Return: Form MGT-7 & MGT-7A
question_text: What is the statutory deadline for filing the Annual Return (Form MGT-7/MGT-7A) with the ROC following the AGM?
explanation: Section 92(4) mandates that every company shall file its Annual Return in Form MGT-7/MGT-7A within sixty days from the date on which the annual general meeting is held.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 92, Section 88, Companies Act, 2013 & Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014

title: Significant Beneficial Ownership (SBO - Section 90 & BEN-2)
question_text: What is the threshold of indirect/direct shareholding or voting rights that defines a Significant Beneficial Owner (SBO) under Rule 2(1)(h)?
explanation: Rule 2(1)(h) defines an SBO as an individual who, acting alone or together through one or more persons/trusts, possesses not less than 10 per cent of shares, voting rights, or distributable dividends.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 90, Companies Act, 2013 & Companies (Significant Beneficial Owners) Rules, 2018

title: FEMA & Foreign Investment Post-Incorporation Compliances
question_text: Within how many days from the date of allotment of equity shares to a foreign investor must Form FC-GPR be filed on the RBI FIRMS portal?
explanation: Under FEMA NDI Rules, Form FC-GPR must be filed with the Reserve Bank of India through the FIRMS portal within 30 days from the date of allotment of shares.

regulatory_reference.provision: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 & FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019

title: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR - Section 135)
question_text: Which of the following is an eligibility trigger for mandatory CSR compliance under Section 135(1) of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.text: Net Profit of ₹1 Crore or more
Net Profit of ₹5 Crores or more
Paid-up Capital of ₹50 Crores or more

explanation: Section 135(1) applies to any company having Net Worth of ₹500 Cr or more, or Turnover of ₹1,000 Cr or more, or Net Profit of ₹5 Cr or more in the immediately preceding financial year.

regulatory_reference.provision: Section 135, Companies Act, 2013 & Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014

option_a: Net Profit of ₹1 Crore or more
option_b: Net Profit of ₹5 Crores or more
option_d: Paid-up Capital of ₹50 Crores or more
